column1: # stdlib/caps.tsv — what each runtime function does, as a capability class
# A certificate's N.cap claim proves which of a program's functions a run can
# enter (formal/C/Caps.lean); what those functions can do outside the
# program's memory is read off their calls in the core IR, down to the
# runtime functions below, and this table gives each one's class. It is a
# trust row of every certificate that claims N.cap (`caps-table`): a row
# that understates what a function does would let a claim say "never" of
# something the program can do. So a row errs wide: a function that may
# create a file is fs.write even when most calls only read.
# Format: symbol<TAB>class<TAB>what it does. A symbol ending in `*` covers
# every name it is a prefix of (the compiler's own built-ins, which no
# foreign declaration names); the longest prefix wins. A symbol with no
# row reaches the claim as `ffi.unknown`, a door the claim names.
# tools/check_caps_table.sh fails when a foreign (`&`) declaration of the
# standard library has no exact row here.
